name: Danish Power
tagline: Debt-free transformer maker with a genuine 5-year Coffee-Can track record, but the order book is smaller than initially stated and the EHV ramp carries real execution risk
verdict_headline: Exceptional 5-year Coffee-Can track record and a debt-free capacity-expansion story, tempered by a smaller-than-thought order book, SME-platform listing, and a near-term working-capital/margin dip
verdict_reasoning: Four-box score 3.0 (tailwind yes, tam yes, moat weak, valuation weak) permits 10x-in-2-3-years, but conviction set separately

FY22-FY26 all five fiscal years cleared the Coffee-Can test (revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15%) -- a genuinely strong, verified persistence signal, with the company also essentially debt-free (borrowings ~Rs2cr)

But the confirmed+unexecuted order book (~Rs900cr, ~1.7x FY26 revenue) is materially smaller than the EUR500mn/~9x-revenue figure in the prior light-pass note -- a meaningful correction to the growth-visibility thesis

Growth has decelerated every year since the FY24 spike (+77% FY24 -> +28% FY25 -> +22% FY26), EBITDA margin dipped to ~17% FY26 from 19% FY25 on capacity-expansion cost drag, and working capital stretched from 78 to 102 days with negative FY25 operating cash flow (-Rs20cr)
Listed on the NSE SME platform (not mainboard) with correspondingly thinner institutional access; 220kV EHV revenue realistically a FY28 story pending type-testing/customer-audit validation
business_overview: Danish Power (Jaipur, founded 1985 by Dinesh Talwar, now led by second-generation MD Shivam Talwar) manufactures inverter-duty transformers (IDTs, ~70% of revenue) for solar/wind, plus distribution and power transformers up to 100 MVA, expanding into 220kV EHV. Listed on NSE SME in Oct 2024 (IPO raised Rs197.90cr). Early mover in IDTs with ~10-11% market share and 14GW of solar projects powered.
fundamentals_table: ~23-24% FY25/26 (down from a 70% FY23 IPO-year spike; 3yr avg ~45.2%)
~17% (down from 19% FY25 on capacity-expansion cost drag)
~500 confirmed (90% executable FY27) + ~400 unexecuted (Dec 2025) -- NOT the ~EUR500mn figure in the earlier light-pass note, which appears overstated
~8,500 MVA (Oct 2025, 96% utilization) -> ~11,000 MVA (Dec 2025 Phase 2) -> targeting 12,000-15,000 MVA, enabling 220kV EHV

fundamentals_narrative: Danish Power has compounded revenue from Rs118cr (FY21) to Rs521cr (FY26), a ~35% 5yr CAGR, with PAT growing faster still (~103% 5yr CAGR) as EBITDA margin structurally expanded from 3.6% to 17-19%. Every single fiscal year FY22-FY26 cleared both Coffee-Can bars (revenue growth >=10% and ROCE >=15%), including a 70% ROCE in the IPO year (FY23) that has since normalized to a still-healthy ~23-24%. The balance sheet is essentially debt-free (borrowings ~Rs2cr), capacity has nearly doubled (8,500 -> 11,000 MVA) funded without leverage, and the company initiated its first dividend in Sep 2026. But growth has decelerated every year since the FY24 spike (+77% -> +28% -> +22%), EBITDA margin dipped to ~17% in FY26 on capacity-expansion cost drag, working capital stretched from 78 to 102 days, and operating cash flow was negative in FY25 (-Rs20cr) against a heavy Rs73cr FY26 capex outflow. Crucially, the order book actually visible in filings (~Rs500cr confirmed + ~Rs400cr unexecuted, ~1.7x FY26 revenue) is far smaller than the ~EUR500mn figure cited in the prior light-pass four-box note -- that figure looks to have been an error or conflated with an industry-level opportunity size, and this pass corrects it. Management guides FY27 revenue above Rs700cr at ~19% EBITDA margin, with exports scaling toward 20% (FY27) and 30% (FY28), contingent on 220kV type-testing/customer-audit validation (6-8 months) that pushes meaningful EHV revenue to FY28.
bse_notes: May 2026: USD8.7mn export order for 66kV power transformers (1yr execution). Aug 2026: Rs37.17cr order for Ester-Filled Inverter Duty Transformers (5-6mo execution). Separately, Rs84cr export order for 66kV transformers and Rs48.77cr order for inverter-duty transformers reported in 2026. Sep 2026: first post-listing dividend (Rs2/share) declared.
bull_case: Genuine 5-year Coffee-Can track record: every fiscal year FY22-FY26 cleared both revenue growth >=10% and ROCE >=15% (ROCE ranged 23-70%, 3yr avg ~45%) -- a rare, verified consistency signal

Early-mover moat in inverter-duty transformers (~70% of revenue): ~10-11% market share, 14GW of solar projects powered, 14 years of customer-qualification stickiness, BIS-certified quality seen as a natural barrier against Chinese imports

Capacity doubling from ~8,500 MVA to ~11,000 MVA (enabling 220kV EHV) funded almost entirely debt-free (borrowings ~Rs2cr), with management guiding FY27 revenue above Rs700cr (+34%+ YoY) and exports scaling to 20% (FY27) then 30% (FY28)

CRISIL upgraded the rating to BBB+/Positive/A2 in 2025 and the company just initiated its first dividend (Rs2/share, Sep 2026) -- external validation plus early signs of capital-allocation discipline from second-generation MD Shivam Talwar ('profitability over volume, customer quality over order quantity')
bear_case: The order book is materially smaller than the earlier light-pass note implied: ~Rs500cr confirmed + ~Rs400cr unexecuted (~1-1.7x FY26 revenue), not the ~EUR500mn/~9x-revenue figure cited previously -- a meaningful correction to the growth-visibility thesis

Growth has decelerated every year since the FY24 spike (revenue +77% FY24 -> +28% FY25 -> +22% FY26) while ROCE normalized from a 70% IPO-year peak to ~23-24%, and EBITDA margin dipped to ~17% FY26 from 19% FY25 on capacity-expansion cost drag

Working capital deteriorated (78 -> 102 days) and operating cash flow was negative in FY25 (-Rs20cr) despite profitability, with a heavy Rs73cr capex outflow in FY26; the 220kV EHV ramp (type-testing, customer audits, 6-8 month validation) adds further execution risk, realistically pushing full EHV revenue to FY28

Listed on the NSE SME platform (not mainboard) -- thinner institutional access/liquidity than a mainboard small-cap -- and the IDT segment (70% of revenue) faces rising competitive intensity that could pressure margins
Export ambitions (30% of revenue by FY28) look aggressive given tariff uncertainty and the company's lack of US UL certification

key_new_facts: The order book actually visible in filings/announcements (~Rs500cr confirmed + ~Rs400cr unexecuted, ~Rs900cr total, ~1.7x FY26 revenue) is far smaller than the ~EUR500mn (~9x revenue) figure cited in the prior light-pass four-box note -- this appears to have been an error or a conflation with an industry-level opportunity size, corrected this pass
All five verifiable fiscal years (FY22-FY26) independently clear the Coffee-Can persistence test (growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15%) -- a genuinely strong signal not previously captured in a structured way

220kV EHV capacity requires third-party type testing and customer audits (6-8 months) before meaningful volumes -- realistically a FY28 revenue contributor, not FY27 as the capacity-expansion headline might suggest
open_questions: What exactly drove the EUR500mn order-book figure in the light-pass note, and should other Confluence-100 entries be checked for the same conflation?
Will FY25's negative operating cash flow (-Rs20cr) persist as capex continues, or was it a one-off tied to the Phase 2 capacity build?
How much of the FY26 margin dip (19% -> 17%) is temporary capex-phase drag vs an early sign of IDT-segment competitive pressure?
No clean multi-quarter shareholding-pattern trend or sector-relative working-capital comparison was sourced this pass -- worth revisiting with a direct BSE shareholding filing pull
deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Medium. The genuinely strong 5-year Coffee-Can track record (5/5 years cleared), debt-free balance sheet, CRISIL rating upgrade and first dividend are real positives that argue for holding conviction steady or higher. But this pass also corrected a materially overstated order-book figure from the light-pass note (actual ~Rs900cr vs the ~EUR500mn claimed), surfaced a working-capital/OCF deterioration and FY26 margin dip, and confirmed the NSE SME listing (not mainboard) -- these largely offset the quality upgrade, so conviction holds at Medium rather than moving up.

market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: Revenue toward management's Rs700cr+ guide (+34% YoY) but EBITDA margin likely near the guided ~19% (vs FY26's ~17%), so PAT growth roughly 25-35% if capacity ramps on schedule

market_expectation.gap_basis: Market is already paying a growth multiple (26.8x) for the capacity story, but the EHV/export optionality (FY28-skewed) is not fully priced if execution holds; a slip in type-testing or export certification would likely compress the multiple faster than it would hit near-term earnings

catalyst.event: 220kV type-testing completion + first EHV customer order, plus Q2/Q3 FY27 results confirming margin recovery toward the guided ~19%

value_chain.theme: power/renewable-energy transformer manufacturing (IDT, distribution, power, and emerging EHV up to 220kV)
value_chain.position: component/equipment manufacturer to solar/wind EPCs, grid operators and industrial clients -- early mover in inverter-duty transformers
value_chain.bottleneck_node: CRGO steel sourcing (import-dependent) + EHV type-testing/certification capacity
value_chain.note: Global transformer lead times of 128-144 weeks and India's RE/data-centre buildout are genuine structural demand; Danish Power's capacity add targets this, but it is one of several Indian makers chasing the same shortage-driven opportunity -- limited pricing power beyond the shortage window.

drivers: Scale/mix shift toward EHV + export (higher-margin) as capacity ramps
CRGO steel cost pass-through lag (import-dependent raw material)
FY26 capex-phase cost drag (Rs73cr capex) temporarily compressing margin
earnings_quality.normalised_note: Margin has structurally expanded from 3.6% (FY21) to ~17-19% (FY25-26) as scale and mix improved; FY26's dip to ~17% reads as a capex/ramp-phase cost drag rather than a cyclical peak, consistent with management's 19-21% guided range.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: Revenue YoY: FY22 +26%, FY23 +26%, FY24 +77%, FY25 +28%, FY26 +22% -- growth has decelerated every year since the FY24 spike, though still well above a 10% bar; H1 FY26 revenue Rs211cr/PAT Rs29.31cr was in line with the full-year trajectory.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: At 26.8x trailing P/E (EPS ~Rs35 on Rs69cr PAT), roughly a 25-28% EPS CAGR FY26-28 is needed to justify the multiple at a ~20x steady-state exit; FY27 guidance (revenue Rs700cr+, margin ~19%) implies PAT growth in a similar 25-35% range if execution holds -- a reasonably tight fit, not an obvious mispricing either way.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Capacity expansion funded almost entirely without debt (borrowings ~Rs2cr); IPO proceeds + internal accruals funding the ~Rs73cr FY26 capex; no unrelated diversification
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Explicit move up the value chain from standard IDTs toward 220kV EHV transformers and export markets; management-articulated 'profitability over volume, customer quality over order quantity'

track_record.note: FY22-FY26 all cleared both tests (revenue growth >=10%, ROCE >=15%): growth ranged 22-77% YoY and ROCE ranged 23-70% (FY23 IPO-year figure likely an outlier high, but even the lowest recent years, ~23-24% FY25/26, comfortably clear 15%). A genuinely strong, verified Coffee-Can persistence signal.

four_box.note: tailwind yes (global transformer shortage, 128-144wk lead times, India RE/data-centre + grid buildout -- structural, multi-year); tam yes (capacity near-doubling, export optionality, EHV segment entry); moat weak (IDT early-mover edge + customer stickiness real but several qualified Indian/global EHV makers compete, limited pricing power); valuation weak (26.8x P/E already prices a growth story against a corrected, smaller order book than previously assumed).

shareholding_pattern.note: Only two clean data points sourced this pass (post-IPO and current), not a full quarterly trend -- promoter holding has been essentially flat since listing with no disclosed pledge. FII+DII combined ~4.28% as of Mar 2026 (FII 0.27%, DII 4.01%); no prior-quarter comparison sourced, so fii_dii_pct_trend is unclear rather than a real trend read.

No clean peer (TARIL/Voltamp) comparison was sourced this pass, so sector_relative is left unclear rather than guessed.

scenario_analysis.note: Base case (FY26-28 revenue CAGR ~24% toward the Rs700cr+ FY27 guide, margin recovering to ~19%) implies ~27% upside -- CMP sits closer to base than to bull or bear, consistent with gap_direction 'partially-priced'. Bull needs the EHV/export ramp to execute cleanly with margin reaching 21%; bear assumes type-testing slips and IDT competition compresses margin toward 16%.
